children: Our Bureau New Delhi: AceVector, the parent of ecommerce marketplace Snapdeal, raised 189 crore from anchor investors on September 24, a day ahead of the launch of its initial public offering (IPO), according to a regulatory filing. On its opening day, the IPO got subscribed 23%, with retail investors bidding for 62% of their allocation and non-institutional investors subscribing to 42%.

Domestic investors including Helios Mutual Fund, Singularity Growth and Alchemy Capital participated in the anchor round, picking up shares at 32 apiece. AceVector has set a price band of 30-32 per share for the 420 crore public issue. AceVector is aiming to raise 287 crore in fresh capital, while investors including SoftBank, Nexus Venture Partners and Foxconn are selling shares worth 133 crore through the offer for sale (OFS) component. At the upper end of the price band, the company will get valued at 1,741 crore.

title: Snapdeal Parent Bags 189 cr from Anchor Investors
